TODDLER ROOM LESSON · TODDLER ROOM · AGES 1–3 YEARS

Blanket — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches "blanket" away from bedtime first — the word gets its own happy game, so when it appears at the crib rail it is already a friend.

What is this?

A blanket is the soft cover that goes over the body for sleeping — folded by day, spread over the crib by night, and known to every toddler as the cozy part of bedtime.

What does it mean?

Blanket is a routine word: it does not describe a thing so much as predict an event. Routine words are the toddler’s schedule made speakable.

What does the child need to know?

You need the blanket, a willing teddy and one rule — the game happens when nobody is tired. A word practised in daylight works at night; a word introduced at bedtime works a week later.

Why this matters

Bedtime friction is usually surprise friction. The word "blanket" said at the same moment nightly turns the cover into a countdown the toddler’s body believes.

What it teaches

Routine vocabulary, object permanence (things go under and come back), gentle-hand practice, and the self-soothing habit of a cover that means rest.

Words to learn

blanketsoftcozytucked innight-nightsleep

Say this to your child

“"Blanket! The soft, cozy blanket. Look — teddy is cold! Tuck him in… night-night, teddy. Shhh, he is sleeping. And… good morning, teddy! Again! You tuck him in this time."”

Step by step

  1. Bring the blanket to the play floor: "blanket! Soft and cozy."
  2. Tuck the teddy in: "night-night, teddy" — cover him fully, wait two seconds.
  3. Lift the blanket: "good MORNING, teddy!" The reveal is the joke; do it five times.
  4. Offer the turn: the toddler covers the teddy. Sloppy tucks are perfect tucks.
  5. At bedtime tonight, hold the same blanket and use the same words — "blanket, cozy, night-night" — so the game and the crib speak one language.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "blanket" sits under a folded blue blanket — folded the way it waits on the crib all day before it works at night.

Ask your child

"Where does the blanket go?" (on the bed / over teddy) "Who is sleeping under the blanket?" "Is the blanket soft or hard?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say "nigh-nigh" while tucking, pat the blanket gently, or fetch it at bedtime unprompted — the routine word landing where it lives.

Out in the real world

Blankets live on sofas, in prams, in grandma’s house. Each sighting is a free repetition: "blanket! Cozy one." The word travels; the routine follows.

Try it together

Teddy Tuck-In: three tucks, three wake-ups, then swap roles — the toddler tucks, YOU say night-night. Reversing the roles doubles the giggles and the practice.

Understanding check

Ask: "Where does the blanket go?" (on the bed) "Show me soft." (a gentle pat) "Who sleeps under it?" A pat, a point, a name — the sleepy word is won.

This lesson pairs with the Blanket flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Toddler Room.
